## What this is

1.4.1 fixes one thing, on the Settings page, and tidies the language folders. The engine, the file format, the REST API, the MCP server and every other screen are what 1.4.0 has.

## The Settings page keeps what you changed

Every Save on the Settings page is answered with the settings as the server has them. If you changed a field after pressing Save and before that answer came back, the answer put the field back to the value you had just left, with no message. An admin who saved and then changed the next field right away could lose that change.

Now a field that still holds what was sent takes the server's value, and a field you edited since keeps your edit. A browser test holds the answer back for a second and a half and changes a field in between. On 1.4.0's page it fails (it shows the first value where the second was set), and on this page it passes.

## The language folders

The `_review.json` lists in each language folder are gone, and so is the build check that read them. Nothing else read them, and no native-speaker review is planned. The translations are what 1.4.0 shipped.

## amd64 only, and why

This release builds amd64 only. Multi-arch ships in its own run, so the release after this one is a single small version bump that builds both. `stable`, `latest`, `1.4` and `1` list the new amd64 image beside the arm64 image they already pointed at.

## Upgrading, and going back

No migrations: the schema is the one 1.4.0 has. `helm upgrade` to 1.4.1, or let `:stable` roll the Quadlet units. Putting 1.4.0 back is safe, because nothing in the database changed.
